title: Mallow and Snug's Wiggle Blanket
markdown:
Mallow the mouse wiggled his little pink nose. His whiskers twitched this way and that, tickling the air. Snug the teddy sat right beside him, his two shiny button eyes watching Mallow with a kind gaze. They were in their favourite play corner, a soft spot filled with sunny light and the smell of warm fabric.

Mallow pointed with a little paw at the blanket’s corner. It would not stay. It liked to lift, and flop, and wander.

“This blanket corner,” he squeaked, in a tiny happy voice. “It likes to wiggle and jiggle.”

Snug hummed a soft comforting tune, a low rumbling sound that made Mallow feel extra safe. He reached out and gently patted the fluffy blanket with his soft paw. Just as he did, the corner wiggled like a little jig and then — plop — it tickled its way onto the floor.

“Boop,” said Mallow, his whiskers quivering. “It wiggled again. It likes to play peek-a-boo.”

They both loved their soft warm blanket very much. It was perfect for snuggling and for building forts. They wanted the cosy corner to stay in place, neat and happy.

“Let’s help it stay put, Snug,” squeaked Mallow, and his tail did a little happy flick. “We’ll make it play nicely.”

Snug nodded his fluffy head, a slow steady nod. “Help it, Mallow. Yes,” he hummed.

Mallow scampered around the play corner. His bright eyes searched until he found a little piece of soft colourful string. It was a beautiful blue, the very same colour as the sky on a perfectly sunny day. The string felt smooth between his tiny paws.

Snug held the blanket corner steady with his big soft paws. Mallow, using his nimble ones, began to work. He used the blue string to gently tie the corner, tucking it in just so.

“Hold it nice and steady, Snug,” squeaked Mallow, concentrating hard. He tied a little knot. A perfect little knot. “There. All done.”

The blanket corner stayed tucked in. It did not flop onto the floor. Mallow clapped his tiny paws. Snug gave a deep happy hum.

Mallow looked at the tucked-in corner. It stood up a little, straight and proud. It looked, he thought, a little like a tiny sail on a boat. A very small, very cosy boat, ready for a quiet sort of adventure.

“Look, Snug,” squeaked Mallow, his eyes twinkling. “It’s a sail. A special cosy sail.”

Snug looked, really looked. He wiggled his fuzzy ears, which always meant he was thinking happy thoughts. “A sail,” he hummed, a big smile in his voice.

Mallow pretended to be a brave little captain, standing tall on the soft blanket. Snug was the steady ship. The little blanket corner, their special fixed sail, stood up tall, catching the gentle breeze of their play.

The wind of their games made the sail wiggle just a tiny bit, a happy dance. It was the best sail. The corner stayed put, and their playtime felt extra extra fun.

They loved their cosy play corner even more now, with its smart steady sail. Outside the window the sunny light moved a little, and the blue string held, and the blanket, which had liked to wander, stayed and went voyaging all the same.
